content.text: {"findings":[{"status":"open","category":"checker_error_spec_mismatch","evidence":"P10 support_status says 'one-cycle tolerance, boundary values unresolved', but the SCOPE text and finalize() enforce strict lower bounds with no tolerance. finalize() also marks a configuration-change gap in [max(old,new), old+new) as BLOCKING unresolved, while P10 says the additive reading is 'reported but not enforced'.","impact":"The property table and the code disagree. The checker cannot be frozen until one definition of switch timing is chosen and cited. The additive old+new reading has real support in theory_of_operation 326-329 ('before and after'), so treating it as unresolved rather than as a failure needs justification."},{"status":"open","category":"false_positive_control","evidence":"negative/software_reset_not_idle mutates post.active at cycle 18 and still returns scoped_pass. The checker never checks active. P04 starts checking only from the second consecutive sw_reset cycle, so a single-cycle sw_reset pulse is never checked.","impact":"This control does not demonstrate detection. The software-reset separation property has no effective negative control and is weak for single-cycle resets. Either replace the control with one that mutates csb or wr/rd on a held reset cycle, or declare active as out of scope and drop the control."},{"status":"open","category":"false_positive_control","evidence":"negative/last_read_without_transfer sets pre.last_read=1 with no rd pulse and returns scoped_pass. By design, last flags are constrained only on handshake edges.","impact":"The result is consistent with the declared scope, but the control is mislabeled as a negative. It must be reclassified as a scope-confirming control, not counted as detection evidence."},{"status":"open","category":"checker_error_event_qualification","evidence":"negative/clock_moves_during_stall and negative/asynchronous_reset_wrong_select both still emit qualified events (backpressure_then_recovery; abort_then_restart). For stall, the release precedes the injected failure check: the nf snapshot is taken at stall start, yet the event still emitted. For abort, failures raised during the reset row occur before do_reset records nf.","impact":"Events are counted even when the trace contains a violation inside the event window. Event qualification must require zero failures across the whole event window, including the reset rows. As implemented, these events are false positives."},{"status":"open","category":"possible_spec_violation_vs_instrumentation","evidence":"In configuration_switch, the old segment (csid 0, CSAAT) is followed by a config-changed offer at cycle 49 (clkdiv 1, idle/lead/trail 2, cpol 1). In the captured row: pre.ready=1, csb=2 in both pre and post, and post.sck goes 0->1, the toggle toward the new CPOL while CSB[0] is still low. The select stays low through cycle 119. There is no all-high gap, so the checker reports switch_fresh_idle.","impact":"If the excerpt is a faithful capture, this contradicts theory_of_operation 241, 246-249 and 323-324: the configuration should apply only after all CSB are high, and CPOL should not change while selected. That makes it a candidate specification violation. It cannot be classified as a DUT defect without three things: the full trace, adapter/probe review (are the config fields routed to the FSM correctly, and is csb mapped and sampled correctly), and RTL review. The csid_switch case passes with a 1-cycle gap, so the instrumentation mapping of csb is at least partly validated."},{"status":"open","category":"unsupported_assumption","evidence":"enough() requires total*16/lanes SCK edges. This assumes 8 bits per byte at 1/2/4 lanes, 2 edges per bit, and that every edge is attributed to the oldest open segment. P15 itself says the edge-to-byte relation is not fixed by the cited text.","impact":"This is used as a completion criterion for all three event families. It is plausible but not cited. An RTL or spec citation is needed, or it should be declared an explicit modelling assumption."},{"status":"open","category":"checker_error","evidence":"In the switch logic, trail is measured from st['last_edge'], which is updated by any SCK edge while any select is active. CPOL-change edges and edges belonging to the new segment while the old select is low are not distinguished. Lead is taken as the first edge after the fall, without checking that the edge belongs to the new CSID.","impact":"Trail and lead measurement may misattribute edges in queued or overlapping cases. This needs a negative control in which a late spurious edge precedes the release."},{"status":"open","category":"missed_negative_control","evidence":"The controls list has no mutations for: short trail or lead in a switch; a stale byte after async reset (only the sw-reset stale self-test exists); a spurious idle SCK against CPOL; a wrong target select outside a switch; a CSB change during stall; rd without rx_ready; or a config switch with insufficient additive idle.","impact":"Several implemented properties have no demonstrated detection on DUT-derived traces."},{"status":"open","category":"unresolved_scope","evidence":"A software reset coincident with stall suspends checking and is blocking unresolved. The enable input is unused. Dummy segments are excluded from switches. Liveness is never failed.","impact":"These are acceptable as explicit unresolved items. Whether reset takes precedence over stall needs RTL or further specification. No event in the stall+reset combination may be claimed."},{"status":"info","category":"event_family_qualification","evidence":"backpressure_then_recovery: tx, rx and tx_rx calibrations emit events. abort_then_restart: separate sw_reset and async_reset events. constrained_transaction_switch: only csid_change is qualified; config_change yields no event because of the suspected violation.","impact":"backpressure_then_recovery and abort_then_restart are qualifiable once event-window failure gating is fixed and effective negatives are added. Software-reset negatives are currently ineffective. constrained_transaction_switch is qualified only for the CSID-change kind. The configuration-change kind cannot be qualified until the cycle-49 behavior is adjudicated, which requires RTL or adapter review, and until the P10 timing definition is settled."},{"status":"info","category":"documentation_mismatch","evidence":"The LEN width is 8 bits in theory_of_operation 132 and 20 bits in registers.md and the interface. The mismatch is disclosed.","impact":"No further action is needed beyond keeping the disclosure."}],"ready_to_freeze":false,"required_followup":["Reconcile the P10 text with the code: decide on tolerance, and on whether the additive old+new idle gap is enforced, unresolved, or a failure.","Gate all event emission on zero failures over the full event window, including reset rows and stall rows, then rerun the clock_moves_during_stall and asynchronous_reset_wrong_select controls.","Replace or relabel the ineffective controls software_reset_not_idle and last_read_without_transfer. Add a single-cycle sw_reset check or explicitly scope it out.","Add negative controls for: switch trail/lead short; additive idle short; async-reset stale byte; spurious idle SCK; CSB change during stall; rd without rx_ready.","Adjudicate configuration_switch cycle 49 with the full trace plus adapter/probe review and RTL review before labelling it a DUT specification violation versus instrumentation error.","Cite or explicitly declare the edges-per-byte completion assumption (16/lanes); confirm it against RTL.","Resolve sw_reset-during-stall precedence and enable semantics via RTL or further specification; keep these unresolved until then.","Verify that trail/lead edge attribution only counts edges belonging to the old/new select respectively."]}
